euoplocephalus:eswiki:17.title: Euoplocephalus tutus (Sentidos y el flujo de aire)

facts.statement: The first fossil of Euoplocephalus was discovered in Alberta in 1897.
facts.quote: The first fossil of Euoplocephalus was found in 1897 in Alberta.

facts.statement: The genus was originally named Stereocephalus in 1902 but was renamed Euoplocephalus in 1910 because the original name was already used for an insect.
facts.quote: In 1902, it was named Stereocephalus, but that name had already been given to an insect, so it was changed in 1910.

facts.statement: In 1971, Walter Coombs concluded that many previously separate ankylosaurid genera belonged to Euoplocephalus, making it one of the best-known dinosaurs at the time.
facts.quote: In 1971, Walter Coombs concluded that they all belonged to Euoplocephalus, which then make it one of the best-known dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Recent experts have limited the number of authentic Euoplocephalus specimens to about a dozen, reversing the earlier broad classification by Walter Coombs.
facts.quote: Recently, however, experts have come to the opposite conclusion, limiting the authentic finds of Euoplocephalus to about a dozen specimens.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus was a large herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Canada during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus ( ) is a genus of large herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaurs, living during the Late Cretaceous of Canada.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus reached a length of 5.3 meters and a body mass of 2 metric tons.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus reached 5.3 m in length and 2 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus had a low-slung, very flat and wide body that stood on four sturdy legs.
facts.quote: Its body was low-slung and very flat and wide, standing on four sturdy legs.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus had a short, drooping snout equipped with a horny beak used to bite off plants for digestion in its large gut.
facts.quote: Its head had a short drooping snout with a horny beak to bite off plants that were digested in the large gut.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus was largely covered in bony armor plates, including rows of large, high-ridged oval scutes.
facts.quote: Like other ankylosaurids, Euoplocephalus was largely covered by bony armor plates, among them rows of large high-ridged oval scutes.

facts.statement: The neck of Euoplocephalus was protected by two rings of bone.
facts.quote: The neck was protected by two bone rings.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus was approximately 5.3 meters long and weighed about 2 metric tons.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus was about 5.3 m long and weighed about 2 MT.

facts.statement: The premaxillae, or front snout bones, of Euoplocephalus are not covered by dermal ossifications.
facts.quote: The premaxillae, the front snout bones, are not covered by dermal ossifications.

facts.statement: The largest known skull of Euoplocephalus, specimen AMNH 5403, measures 411 millimeters in length and 478 millimeters in width.
facts.quote: The largest known skull, that of specimen AMNH 5403, has a length of 411 millimetres and a width of 478 millimetres.

facts.statement: The teeth of Euoplocephalus are very small, with a maximum height and width of just 7.5 millimeters.
facts.quote: The teeth are very small, with a maximal height and width of just 7.5 millimetres.

facts.statement: Each side of the Euoplocephalus skull has two external nostrils.
facts.quote: Each side has two external nostrils.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Euoplocephalus has a very concave upper rim containing twenty-one teeth.
facts.quote: The lower jaw has a very concave upper rim with twenty-one teeth.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus has at least twenty-one caudal vertebrae, but the total is uncertain as approximately ten are fused to form the tail club, bringing the estimated total to about thirty.
facts.quote: There are at least twenty-one caudal vertebrae; the total number of caudal vertebrae is uncertain because approximately ten are fused to form part of the tail club, bringing the total to about thirty.

facts.statement: Although not well known, the foot of Euoplocephalus was functionally tridactyl with hoof-shaped toes instead of sharp claws.
facts.quote: The foot is not well known but functionally tridactyl with hoof-shaped instead of sharp claws.

facts.statement: The taxonomic name for this animal is Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: taxon: Euoplocephalus

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus was described by Lambe in 1910.
facts.quote: authority: Lambe, 1910

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Euoplocephalus is Euoplocephalus tutus.
facts.quote: type_species: Euoplocephalus tutus

facts.statement: The type species Euoplocephalus tutus was originally described by Lambe in 1902.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Lambe, 1902

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus is classified as a genus of large herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus ( ) is a genus of large herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaurs

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the number of valid Euoplocephalus specimens, with some experts accepting many remains while others limit them to about a dozen.
facts.quote: In 1971, Walter Coombs concluded that they all belonged to Euoplocephalus, which then make it one of the best-known dinosaurs. Recently, however, experts have come to the opposite conclusion, limiting the authentic finds of Euoplocephalus to about a dozen specimens.

facts.statement: The form and function of the complex air passages and sinuses in the Euoplocephalus snout are not yet completely understood.
facts.quote: the form and function of which are not yet completely understood

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus had bony armor covering its head and body, excluding parts of the limbs and possibly the tail tip.
facts.quote: The head and body of Euoplocephalus were covered with bony armor, except for parts of the limbs and possibly the distal tail.

facts.statement: The armor of Euoplocephalus was made of osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin rather than part of the internal skeleton.
facts.quote: The armor consisted of osteoderms, skin ossifications that are not part of the skeleton proper.

facts.statement: Much of Euoplocephalus's armor consisted of hundreds of small, round bony scutes less than five millimeters in diameter.
facts.quote: Much of the armor was made up of small ossicles, bony round scutes with a diameter of less than five millimetres, of which often hundreds have been found with a single specimen.

facts.statement: Larger oval, flat, or keeled scutes were arranged in horizontal rows within the transverse bands of the armor.
facts.quote: Inset in these bands were horizontal rows of larger oval, flat or keeled, scutes.

facts.statement: Some shoulder osteoderms of Euoplocephalus found in specimen ROM 1930 had a base length of fifteen centimeters.
facts.quote: ROM 1930 includes some osteoderms with a base length of fifteen centimeters.

facts.statement: Large keeled plates covered the upper arms of Euoplocephalus, with one specimen preserving a round osteoderm twenty centimeters in diameter and spikes on the lower arm.
facts.quote: Large keeled plates were present on the upper arms as shown by specimen TMP 1997.132.01 conserving a round osteoderm near the humerus with a diameter of twenty centimeters and narrower spikes associated with the lower arm.

facts.statement: Each cervical half-ring of Euoplocephalus was constructed from six rectangular concave plates, with three on each side.
facts.quote: Each half-ring is constructed out of six rectangular concave plates, three per side.

facts.statement: The caputegulae on the snout of Euoplocephalus formed a chaotic and asymmetric mosaic pattern.
facts.quote: On the snout they form a chaotic and asymmetric mosaic.

facts.statement: A large, tongue-shaped quadratojugal osteoderm projected below the lower rear side of the Euoplocephalus skull.
facts.quote: At the lower rear side of the skull, a quadratojugal horn is present, in the form of an enormous tongue-shaped osteoderm projecting below.

facts.statement: Lawrence Morris Lambe discovered the first Euoplocephalus specimen on August 18, 1897, in the Red Deer River valley near present-day Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Canadian paleontologist Lawrence Morris Lambe discovered the first specimen on 18 August 1897 in the area of the present Dinosaur Provincial Park, in the valley of the Red Deer River, Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: The first Euoplocephalus specimen, CMN 210, was designated as the holotype for the species Stereocephalus tutus in 1902.
facts.quote: In 1902, this fossil, CMN 210 (also NMC 210) was designated as the holotype specimen of the type species Stereocephalus tutus.

facts.statement: Lawrence Morris Lambe renamed the genus Euoplocephalus in 1910 because the original name was already taken by an insect.
facts.quote: Lambe changed it to Euoplocephalus in 1910, with as combinatio nova (new combination name) Euoplocephalus tutus.

facts.statement: Edwin Hennig classified Euoplocephalus tutus under the genus Palaeoscincus in 1915.
facts.quote: In 1915, Edwin Hennig classified E. tutus under the genus Palaeoscincus Leidy 1856, coining Palaeoscincus tutus.

facts.statement: The genus Palaeoscincus is now considered a nomen dubium due to its basis on indeterminate ankylosaurian teeth.
facts.quote: Today however, Palaeoscincus is considered to be a nomen dubium based on indeterminate ankylosaurian teeth.

facts.statement: Oskar Kuhn referred Euoplocephalus to the genus Ankylosaurus in 1964, naming it Ankylosaurus tutus.
facts.quote: In 1964, Euoplocephalus was by Oskar Kuhn referred to Ankylosaurus, as a Ankylosaurus tutus.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus tutus is the only valid species currently recognized within the genus Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: The only valid species known today is Euoplocephalus tutus.

facts.statement: Walter Coombs published a landmark re-appraisal of North American ankylosaurs in his 1971 dissertation.
facts.quote: In 1971 however, Walter Coombs submitted a dissertation containing a landmark re-appraisal of North American ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: Walter Coombs included the Asian ankylosaurid Tarchia in the genus Euoplocephalus in 1978, renaming it Euoplocephalus giganteus.
facts.quote: In 1978, Coombs even included the Asian ankylosaurid Tarchia in the genus, renaming it as Euoplocephalus giganteus.

facts.statement: A 2009 study validated Dyoplosaurus as a distinct taxon from Euoplocephalus, noting unique features like triangular claws.
facts.quote: A 2009 study found that Dyoplosaurus is in fact a valid taxon, and identified unique characteristics that differentiated it from Euoplocephalus, including its triangular claws.

facts.statement: Paul Penkalski and William T. Blows re-validated the genus Scolosaurus in a 2013 study.
facts.quote: The first, published by Paul Penkalski and William T. Blows in 2013, re-validated Scolosaurus as well.

facts.statement: Paul Penkalski named and described the new genus Oohkotokia in 2013 based on remains previously attributed to Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: The second study, by Penkalski (2013), named and described Oohkotokia from Montana on the basis of remains that were originally thought to be referable to Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: Victoria Arbour limited the reliable specimens of Euoplocephalus to the lowest thirty meters of the Dinosaur Park Formation in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013 Arbour limited the specimens that could be reliably referred to Euoplocephalus to the lowest thirty metres of the Dinosaur Park Formation.

facts.statement: The banded arrangement of Euoplocephalus's armor is thought to have allowed for some freedom of movement.
facts.quote: The banded arrangement is thought to have permitted some freedom of movement.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the cervical half-rings of Euoplocephalus were fused osteoderms or a lower layer of ossified cartilage, as suggested by Arbour et al. in 2013.
facts.quote: Earlier seen as a fusion of osteoderms, this was doubted by Arbour et al. in 2013, who pointed out that they formed a lower layer, possibly consisting of ossified cartilage, as indicated by a smooth surface and a woven bone texture.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding whether the variation in Euoplocephalus skulls represents multiple species or individual variation within a single species.
facts.quote: He noted that, among the many specimens similar to Euoplocephalus, their skulls varied so much that either every known specimen must be a new species, or they all represented individual variation within a single species: Euoplocephalus tutus.

facts.statement: The armor of Euoplocephalus may have formed a pavement-like structure with transverse bands if configured similarly to the genus Scolosaurus.
facts.quote: If the armor was configured in an identical way to that of Scolosaurus, many of these small ossicles had fused into a kind of pavement, forming transverse bands on the body.

facts.statement: The largest and tallest scutes of Euoplocephalus may have been located on the shoulders, with some reaching a base length of fifteen centimeters.
facts.quote: Types of large scutes varied by body region. It might be that the scutes on the shoulder, near the midline of the body, were largest and tallest; ROM 1930 includes some osteoderms with a base length of fifteen centimeters.

facts.statement: The nuchal crest of Euoplocephalus was covered by two osteoderms on each side between the squamosal horns.
facts.quote: Between them the nuchal crest is covered by two osteoderms per side.

facts.statement: Charles Whitney Gilmore assigned Euoplocephalus to the family Ankylosauridae in 1917.
facts.quote: In 1917, Charles Whitney Gilmore assigned it to the Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus is classified as an ankylosaurid within the suborder Ankylosauria, rather than the Stegosauria.
facts.quote: Today, Euoplocephalus is still seen as an ankylosaurid, but as a member of the Ankylosauria, not the Stegosauria.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus is likely a member of the derived subgroup Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: It is likely also a member of the derived subgroup Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: The genus Euoplocephalus was named by Lambe in 1910.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Lambe, 1910

facts.statement: The species Euoplocephalus tutus was named by Lambe in 1902.
facts.quote: species_authority: Lambe, 1902

facts.statement: Historically, Euoplocephalus fossils were thought to date from 76.5 to 67 million years ago, spanning the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus, following the synonymizations proposed by Coombs (1971), was thought to exist for far longer, and was a member of more distinct faunas, than any of its contemporaries, as these fossils dated to between 76.5 and 67 million years ago in the Campanian-Maastrichtian ages of the late Cretaceous period

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus lived in North America during the late Cretaceous, approximately 76.5 to 75.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 76,5 y 75,4 millones de años, en el Campaniense en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus fossils have been found in the Dinosaur Park and Horseshoe Canyon Formations of Alberta, the Two Medicine Formation of Montana, and possibly the Oldman Formation of Alberta.
facts.quote: and came from the Dinosaur Park and Horseshoe Canyon Formations of Alberta, Two Medicine Formation of Montana, and possibly from the Oldman Formation of Alberta.

facts.statement: Coombs suggested that Euoplocephalus may have possessed running abilities comparable to modern rhinoceroses and hippopotamuses.
facts.quote: According to Coombs, Euoplocephalus may have had cursorial abilities on par with those of the modern rhinoceros and hippopotamus.

facts.statement: The discovery of Euoplocephalus as isolated elements or partial skeletons suggests the animal lived solitarily or in small groups.
facts.quote: Coombs and Maryanska (1990) observed that Euoplocephalus specimens are usually discovered as isolated elements or partial skeletons, which suggested that this animal engaged in solitary habits and was usually either solitary or participated in small group clusters.

facts.statement: The heavily vascularized armor of Euoplocephalus may have played a role in thermoregulation.
facts.quote: In addition to protection, the heavily vascularized armor may have had a role in thermoregulation.

facts.statement: A 2009 study concluded that large ankylosaurian tail clubs could generate enough force to break bone during impacts.
facts.quote: A 2009 study concluded that "large ankylosaurian clubs could generate sufficient force to break bone during impacts, while average and small ones could not".

facts.statement: While tail swinging is feasible in ankylosaurids, it is unknown whether the tail was used for defense against predators, combat between individuals, or both.
facts.quote: It has also concluded that "tail swinging behavior is feasible in ankylosaurids, but it remains unknown whether the tail was used for interspecific defense, intraspecific combat, or both".

facts.statement: The tail club of Euoplocephalus could be swung low to strike the metatarsals or shin bones of attacking theropods.
facts.quote: The tail club could be swung low, toward the fragile metatarsals or shin bones of attacking theropods.

facts.statement: Complex respiratory passages in the skull suggest Euoplocephalus had a good sense of smell.
facts.quote: The complex respiratory passages observed in the skull suggest that Euoplocephalus had a good sense of smell

facts.statement: A 2011 study found that Euoplocephalus had looped, complex nasal passages with an enlarged vascularized chamber, possibly adapted to improve its sense of smell.
facts.quote: A 2011 study found that the nasal passages of Euoplocephalus were looped and complex; possibly an adaptation for heat and water balance and vocal resonance, and researchers discovered an enlarged and vascularised chamber at the back of the nasal tract, which was considered by the authors to be an adaptation to improve its sense of smell.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Euoplocephalus's inner ear structure was an adaptation for hearing low-toned resonant sounds produced by its nasal passages.
facts.quote: They suggested that this may have been an adaption to hearing low-toned resonant sounds produced by the nasal passages.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus is thought to have been a herbivore.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus, like other ankylosaurians, is thought to have been a herbivore.

facts.statement: Georg Haas (1969) concluded that despite their large size, the jaw muscles of Euoplocephalus skulls were relatively weak.
facts.quote: Georg Haas (1969) examined the evidence for the jaw muscles of two skulls (AMNH 5337 and 5405) and concluded that despite the large size of the skulls the associated musculature was relatively weak.

facts.statement: A 2014 study found that ankylosaurs like Euoplocephalus could eat tough fibrous plant material, though less efficiently than nodosaurids, ceratopsians, or hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: A study conducted in 2014 found that the ankylosaurs were capable of eating of tough fibrous plant material, though not to the same degree as their nodosaur relatives or the ceratopsians and hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Recent studies have debated the attribution of fossils, referring Horseshoe Canyon specimens to Anodontosaurus and Two Medicine specimens to Oohkotokia.
facts.quote: However, recent studies referred all Horseshoe Canyon Formation specimens to Anodontosaurus, and all Two Medicine Formation specimens to Oohkotokia.

facts.statement: The recent splitting of Campanian ankylosaurid material has complicated the determination of Euoplocephalus's direct affinities.
facts.quote: The recent splitting of the ankylosaurid Campanian material of North America has complicated the issue of the direct affinities of Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus measured approximately 5.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 2.5 tons.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus medía aproximadamente 5,5 metros de largo y pesaba aproximadamente 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Its body was wide at 2.4 meters from side to side, deep at approximately 1.20 meters in height, and stood on four short, powerful legs.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo era ancho, 2,4 metros de lado a lado, profundo, de aproximadamente 1,20 metros de altura, colocado sobre cuatro patas cortas y poderosas.

facts.statement: Like all ankylosaurids, it had a flat, thick, and triangular skull.
facts.quote: Como todos los anquilosáuridos, tenía un cráneo plano, grueso y triangular.

facts.statement: It was covered in bands of armor that allowed for remarkable flexibility.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus estaba cubierto con bandas de armaduras, que permitieron una asombrosa flexibilidad.

facts.statement: It was the first ankylosaurid discovered to have armored eyelids that could close to cover its eyes.
facts.quote: Fue el primer anquilosáurido descubierto con los párpados acorazados que podían cerrarse para cubrir sus ojos.

facts.statement: Each piece of armor consisted of a thick oval plate set into thick surrounding skin studded with small osteoderms about 10 to 15 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Cada trozo de armadura estaba compuesto de una placa oval gruesa, encajada en la gruesa piel circundante tachonada con los osteodermos pequeños de cerca de 10 a 15 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: It had large horns on the back of its head.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus tenía cuernos grandes en la parte posterior de su cabeza.

facts.statement: Its tail was rigid and held suspended in the air, possessing a bony club at its end.
facts.quote: La cola era rígida y la llevaba suspendida en el aire, poseyendo un mazo óseo en su extremo.

facts.statement: Internally, many bones were fused together to support the heavy armor.
facts.quote: Internamente, muchos huesos estaban fundidos juntos para proporcionar la ayuda para la pesada armadura.

facts.statement: In 1990, Walter Coombs and Teresa Maryańska declared that Euoplocephalus could be distinguished by four traits.
facts.quote: Al combinar tales formas, Walter Coombs y Teresa Maryańska declararon en 1990 que Euoplocephalus podía distinguirse según cuatro rasgos.

facts.statement: In 2013, Victoria Arbor and Phil Currie provided a differential diagnosis that distinguished Euoplocephalus from its closest relatives.
facts.quote: En 2013, Victoria Arbor y Phil Currie brindaron un diagnóstico diferencial, que distinguió a Euoplocephalus de sus parientes más cercanos.

facts.statement: When compared to Anodontosaurus and Scolosaurus, Euoplocephalus lacks round osteoderms at the base of the squamosal and quadratojugal horns.
facts.quote: Cuando se compara con Anodontosaurus y Scolosaurus, Euoplocephalus carece de osteodermos redondos en la base de los cuernos escamoso y cuadratojugal.

facts.statement: It differs from Dyoplosaurus in possessing sacral ribs that point outward perpendicularly.
facts.quote: Se diferencia del Dyoplosaurus en poseer costillas sacras que perpendicularmente apuntan hacia afuera.

facts.statement: It differs from Scolosaurus in possessing quill-like osteoderms with a round or oval base on the top and sides of the first middle cervical ring and with a shorter posterior iliac lamina.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de Scolosaurus en que posee osteodermos quillados con una base redonda u ovalada en la parte superior y en los lados del primer medio anillo cervical y con una lámina posterior más corta del ilion.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus differs from Ankylosaurus in having externally directed anterior nasal fossae and lacking a continuous keel between the squamosal horn and the supraorbitals.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus se diferencia de Ankylosaurus en poseer fosas nasales externas dirigidas anteriormente y en carecer de una quilla continua entre el asta escamosa y los supraorbitales.

facts.statement: Most skull elements are completely fused, and two skull openings normally present in dinosaurs, the antorbital fenestra and the upper temporal fenestra, are closed.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los elementos del cráneo están completamente fusionados y dos aberturas de cráneo normalmente presentes con dinosaurios, la fenestra antorbital y la fenestra temporal superior, se han cerrado.

facts.statement: The strongly downturned snout is blunt, wide, and high and is filled with air passages and very complex paranasal sinuses, whose shape and function are not yet fully understood.
facts.quote: El hocico fuertemente caído es romo, ancho y alto y está lleno de pasajes de aire y senos paranasales muy complejos, cuya forma y función aún no se comprenden completamente.

facts.statement: Each side has two external nasal fossae.
facts.quote: Cada lado tiene dos fosas nasales externas.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus had a bony armor covering its head and body, except for parts of the limbs and possibly the distal tail.
facts.quote: La cabeza y el cuerpo de Euoplocephalus estaban cubiertos con una armadura ósea, a excepción de partes de las extremidades y posiblemente la cola distal.

facts.statement: The armor consisted of osteoderms, which are bone formations in the skin that are not part of the skeleton itself.
facts.quote: La armadura consistía en osteodermos, osificaciones de la piel que no forman parte del propio esqueleto.

facts.statement: Some osteoderms found in specimen ROM 1930 had a base length of 15 centimeters.
facts.quote: ROM 1930 incluye algunos osteodermos con una longitud de base de 15 centímetros.

facts.statement: The neck was protected by two bone rings open at the bottom, known as "half cervical rings".
facts.quote: El cuello estaba protegido por dos anillos de hueso, abiertos en la parte inferior, que se llaman "medias anillas cervicales".

facts.statement: Each half ring is constructed of six concave rectangular plates, three on each side.
facts.quote: Cada medio anillo está construido de seis placas cóncavas rectangulares, tres por lado.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus had two pyramid-shaped horns growing from the rear corners of its head.
facts.quote: Euoplocephalus tenía dos "cuernos" con forma de pirámide que crecían desde las esquinas posteriores de su cabeza.

facts.statement: At the lower rear of the skull, a quadratojugal horn is present in the form of a huge tongue-shaped osteoderm projecting downward.
facts.quote: En la parte posterior inferior del cráneo, un cuerno cuadratojugal está presente, en forma de un enorme osteodermo con forma de lengua que se proyecta hacia abajo.

facts.statement: According to Coombs, Euoplocephalus may have been capable of running at speeds comparable to modern rhinoceroses and hippos.
facts.quote: Según Coombs, Euoplocephalus pudo haber tenido la capacidad deo correr a la par con las de los rinocerontes modernos y el hipopótamo.

facts.statement: Coombs and Maryanska (1990) observed that Euoplocephalus specimens are usually found as isolated elements or partial skeletons, suggesting the animal was solitary or lived in small groups.
facts.quote: Coombs y Maryanska en 1990 observaron que los especímenes de Euoplocephalus generalmente se descubren como elementos aislados o esqueletos parciales, lo que sugiere que este animal se involucraba en hábitos solitarios y generalmente era solitario o vivía en grupos pequeños.

facts.statement: Besides protection, the heavily vascularized armor may have played a role in thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Además de la protección, la armadura fuertemente vascularizada puede haber tenido un papel en la termorregulación.

facts.statement: Palpebral bones over the eyes may have provided additional protection for the eyes.
facts.quote: Los huesos palpebrales sobre los ojos pueden haber proporcionado protección adicional para los ojos.

facts.statement: Researchers reconstructed the dinosaur's inner ear and concluded it was capable of hearing low frequencies.
facts.quote: Los investigadores también lograron reconstruir el oído interno del dinosaurio y llegaron a la conclusión de que era capaz de escuchar a bajas frecuencias.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus is believed to have been a herbivore, like other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Se cree que Euoplocephalus , como otros anquilosáuridos, fue un herbívoro.

facts.statement: Wear on teeth and jaw joints suggests that lower jaws retracted during feeding and rotated slightly inward.
facts.quote: El desgaste de los dientes y las articulaciones de la mandíbula, dentro de la mandíbula inferior y en la articulación cuadrada de la mandíbula inferior, sugieren que las mandíbulas inferiores se retraían durante la alimentación, y también giraron ligeramente hacia adentro.

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus belongs to the subfamily Euoplocephalini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Euoplocephalini

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus is classified in the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Euoplocephalus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The armor was widely described in 1982 by Kenneth Carpenter, who relied heavily on the complete specimen NHMUK R5161, the holotype of Scolosaurus, which is no longer considered a synonym of Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: Esta armadura fue descrita ampliamente en 1982 por Kenneth Carpenter, quien, sin embargo, se basó en gran medida en el ejemplar muy completo NHMUK R5161, el holotipo de Scolosaurus, que ya no se considera sinónimo de Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: Arbor et al. (2013) suggested that the half rings formed a lower layer possibly consisting of ossified cartilage, indicated by a smooth surface and bone tissue texture.
facts.quote: Arbor et al. en 2013, señalaron que formaban una capa inferior, que posiblemente consistía en cartílago osificado, según lo indicado por una superficie lisa y una textura tejido óseo.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the armor was configured identically to Scolosaurus, with many small ossicles possibly fused into a pavement forming transverse bands on the body.
facts.quote: Si la armadura estaba configurada de manera idéntica a la de Scolosaurus, muchos de estos pequeños osículos se habían fusionado en una especie de pavimento, formando bandas transversales en el cuerpo.

rejected.statement: Euoplocephalus could actively defend itself against predators such as Albertosaurus, Daspletosaurus, and Gorgosaurus using a heavy club at the end of its tail.
rejected.quote: It could also actively defend itself against predators like Albertosaurus, Daspletosaurus, and Gorgosaurus using a heavy club at the end of its tail.
